question: Bind — ATK, 5v5 full-buy, 1:37 left, no spike. You are at the B Site threshold. One teammate is pushing B Long, another is at Hookah entrance. No defender has been spotted yet. What is your highest-EV play as the B Site entry anchor?

options.label: Hold the B Site entrance tight, clear CT and Back-Site angles before committing, and call for the teammate to come through Hookah while the B Long player pins the flank
options.explication_courte: B Site takes require clearing two simultaneous angles (Hookah window and CT stairs). Anchoring at the threshold, coordinating Hookah + B Long at the same moment, means no single defender can hold both — the entry splits their attention and creates crossfire opportunities.

sources_option.citation: A site take succeeds when attackers hit from two angles simultaneously, forcing the defender to choose which gun to face

options.label: Rush straight onto B Site through the main entrance alone right now to grab space before defenders set up
options.explication_courte: Entering B Site alone without coordinating the Hookah or B Long players gives the defender a 1v1 on a pre-aimed angle — you die and lose the map control for free. Site entries require simultaneous pressure to split defender crosshairs.

sources_option.citation: Solo rushing a site without coordinated pressure hands the defender a free isolated duel on his own pre-aimed corner

options.label: Fire your signature utility to deny the CT angle and create a one-way smoke or flash before entering
options.explication_courte: Using utility to cut the CT angle is a legitimate site-take tool, but spending signature here before the Hookah + B Long players are ready to come through simultaneously wastes the element of surprise and the utility charge.

sources_option.citation: Utility that cuts sightlines accelerates site entry, but spending it before teammates are in position means the defense recovers before the rush follows

options.label: Rotate away from B and stack A with the other two teammates for a number advantage there
options.explication_courte: Abandoning B with two teammates already committed to B Long and Hookah strands them in under-manned fights and cedes the entire B half of the map to the defenders for free. Never pull out of a coordinated hit mid-setup.

sources_option.citation: Pulling out of a coordinated entry mid-setup isolates the players already committed and hands the defense free map territory

explication_longue: B Site on Bind is one of the most coordination-dependent takes in the game because it has two natural entry lanes — Hookah (the window) and B Long — that can be covered by a single well-placed defender if attackers don't hit them simultaneously. As the player anchoring at the B Site threshold, your job is to be the third pressure point: you hold CT and Back-Site angles while the Hookah player comes through the window and the B Long player pins the CT rotation. The moment all three lines activate together, the defender has to choose which gun to face — any choice leaves someone else a free swing. Entering alone before that sync is ready gifts the defender a pre-aimed 1v1 that he wins most of the time. Using utility before teammates are in position wastes the surprise without delivering the coordinated rush behind it. Rotating away from B entirely, mid-commit, is the worst outcome: it leaves two teammates stranded in isolated under-manned fights and surrenders the entire B half of the map without a fight. Wait for the sync, hold your angle, then commit together.

sources.citation: Synchronized entries from two angles deny the defender any safe choice — the coordination is the weapon
